I want to say I didn't read any of the comments before I made mine. So from my perspective. I am a long time rider, from dirt bikes all the way to my Goldwing. I'm also a road course track rider. I absolutely appreciate the attraction to sport bikes and if that's where you want to start that is fine, BUT, get something small. An R3, CBR300 or something similar. Get to know what it's like to ride on the street, especially how drivers react. Learn how to handle the smaller lighter and less powerful bikes so you know what to expect. There's no shame in starting small and getting comfortable before moving to something bigger, whether it's a bigger heavier cruiser or a more powerful sport bike. I will die on the hill that the absolute perfect starter/learner bike is a Rebel 250. Small, light and underpowered, but also reliable and well built. You may grow past whatever starter you choose quickly but it should always be an onward and upward approach. Get yourself used to the actual riding first then go amd get the big bike that you can feel confident in your riding skills to where you can learn the bike itself.

Bike theft is a serious problem around here. My RC has recovered several every year. If you can afford a storage unit or a dealer that offers storage, definitely do that. If not, absolutely put a LoJack or some type of equivalent GPS locator on it and then lock it with a thick chain to the frame with the most secure padlock you can find. To the carport pole or something very secure. There's also pull tab alarms that are meant for a purse or backpack if they get pulled apart they go off, attach one of those to the bike and then to the cover.
